# Map genes to a reproducible reference

SpaMTP resolves gene identifiers using versioned RaMP and HUGO Gene Nomenclature
Committee (HGNC) references from SpaMTPdb, with species metadata from SpaMTPData.
This guide follows a human glioma MSI/Xenium example from identifier mapping
to enrichment, spatial pathway scores, co-regulation and joint RNA/MSI networks. Inspecting
mapping status and measured coverage at each step makes the contributors to
each pathway result explicit.

```{r registry, message=FALSE}
library(SpaMTP)
library(SpatialExperiment)
library(SpaMTPdb)
library(withr)
spaMTPdbGeneReference(metadata = TRUE)
spaMTPdbVersion()
```

## Reference snapshot and species

HGNC uses a fixed quarterly archive, versioned independently of RaMP 3.0.7 and
experiment resources 1.1.0. Mapping supports **Homo sapiens**; mouse-to-human
orthology conversion requires a separate step. SpaMTPData stores species in
`metadata(x)$SpaMTPData`, including nested experiments, so checks also apply
after `altExp()` extraction.

# Gene mapping index and identifier resolution

## Demonstration data and pinned inputs

The examples run during builds on 240 aligned human glioma locations nearest the
coordinate-wise median, selected independently of expression or mapping. All
339 RNA features and paired mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) features are retained;
see `help("vignetteData")`
for the recipe and checksums. Missing references download automatically;
`offline = TRUE` uses local files or verified caches.

The [original integrated archive](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18282678)
contains low-grade glioma tissue with paired matrix-assisted laser
desorption/ionization (MALDI) MSI and a 339-gene Xenium panel aligned across
serial sections. The linked
[study](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-025-03884-4) describes iMScope QT acquisition
with alpha-cyano-4-hydroxycinnamic acid (CHCA) matrix and provides the paired data through
[BioImage Archive S-BIAD1426](https://doi.org/10.6019/S-BIAD1426).
Each paired location is an archived Xenium cell position. The study assigned
the mean registered MSI intensity within 20 micrometres of each cell to that
cell; this vignette retains the cell-level RNA counts and selects 240 paired
positions without further RNA pooling.
The archived `cout_labels` column groups locations as Astro, Mesenchymal,
Neuronal, Oligo or Progenitor. These source labels provide cell-state groups
for descriptive contrasts; the packaged archive does not retain the exact
label-assignment recipe. `sample_id` identifies this single archived section.

`database` holds RaMP tables, `reference` holds HGNC, and `index` joins them.
`version` pins each reference; `mapping` resolves three example IDs.

```{r reference}
database <- loadSpaMTPDatabase(
    c("chem_props", "source_df", "analyte", "analytehaspathway", "pathway",
        "ramp_db_metadata"),
    version = "3.0.7"
)
reference <- spaMTPdbGeneReference(version = "2026.7.7")
index <- buildGeneMappingIndex(database$source_df, gene_reference = reference)
pathway_index <- buildPathwayIndex(database, gene_index = index)
mapping <- mapGeneIdentifiers(
    c("gene_symbol:AATK", "entrez:9625", "gene_symbol:BANK1"),
    index = index
)
mapping
```

## Index fingerprints

The index fingerprints gene identifiers and names. Changed identity assignments
invalidate cached indices. Reordering rows or repeating identical source rows
preserves the fingerprint.
Rebuild older indices with `buildGeneMappingIndex()`.

## Identifier resolution

Supported inputs include current or previous symbols, aliases, Entrez, HGNC,
UniProt and versioned Ensembl gene IDs. Approved symbols take priority over
aliases. A compatible gene-specific ID can resolve a shared protein ID;
conflicting specific IDs quarantine the RaMP record.

`gene_id` stores HGNC identity, `ramp_ids` its non-conflicting RaMP records, and
`canonical_ramp_id` a representative for counting each gene once. For AATK,
the UniProt and Entrez records therefore contribute a union of memberships.
The returned table preserves input order and repeated identifiers, with one
row per supplied ID.

## Mapping status and ambiguity

Inspect `status`, `method`, `candidate_gene_ids` and `candidate_ramp_ids`:

- `not_in_ramp`: HGNC identity is resolved; a usable RaMP record is absent.
- `ambiguous` or `conflicting_ramp_records`: competing identities require review.
- `mapped_ramp_only`: a RaMP record lacks a resolved HGNC identity.

`candidate_ramp_ids` exposes raw candidates. Unresolved or conflicting
competitors keep a shared crossreference ambiguous, even with only one known
HGNC candidate. Unresolved mappings describe reference coverage and identity
ambiguity; biological function requires separate evidence.

# Annotate experiment features without altering expression

## Feature annotation

`spe` contains the low-grade glioma subset; `rna` is its `SPT` experiment.
`annotateGeneIdentifiers()` reads row names and checks `organism`.
`unresolved` selects rows whose status differs from `mapped`.

```{r experiment}
spe <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "human_demo.rds", package = "SpaMTP"))
altExpNames(spe)
spe <- annotateGeneIdentifiers(spe,
    assay = "SPT", index = index,
    organism = "Homo sapiens"
)
rna <- altExp(spe, "SPT")
head(rowData(rna))
mapping_counts <- table(rowData(rna)$spamtp_gene_status)
mapping_counts
unresolved <- rowData(rna)$spamtp_gene_status != "mapped"
rowData(rna)[
    unresolved,
    c("spamtp_gene_symbol", "spamtp_gene_status", "spamtp_gene_ramp_ids")
]
```

## Preserved measurements and unresolved genes

Annotation preserves counts, names, coordinates and paired modalities.
Expression rows that map to the same gene remain separate; resolve these
duplicates before differential analysis. Regional and network workflows
reject conflicting differential statistics for one gene within a cluster.

Of `r nrow(rna)` genes, `r unname(mapping_counts["mapped"])` map,
`r unname(mapping_counts["conflicting_ramp_records"])` have conflicting RaMP
records, and `r unname(mapping_counts["not_in_ramp"])` are absent from RaMP.
The `r sum(unresolved)` unresolved genes remain in the expression object.
The mapping warning records these unresolved identities.

`metadata(rna)$gene_mapping$inputs` retains the complete per-feature
audit, including competing identities. Save `spe` with `saveRDS()` to retain
this audit alongside the annotated experiment.

# Use the whole measured panel as the universe

## Foreground and measured universe

The foreground contains the 20 positive markers with the highest mean area
under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) for the archived
`Oligo` group. `LogNormalize` divides each location by its total measured RNA
count, multiplies by 10,000 and applies the base-2 transform `log2(1 + x)`.
`mean_auc` ranks each gene's separation of this group from the remaining groups.
The measured RNA panel supplies the background; `min_path_size = 5` requires
five mapped members.

```{r enrichment}
spe <- normalizeSMData(spe, "LogNormalize", assay = "SPT", verbose = FALSE)
markers <- findAllDEMs(spe,
    ident = "cout_labels", assay = "SPT",
    assayName = "logcounts", method = "markers", spatial_blocks = 0,
    verbose = FALSE
)
foreground_group <- "Oligo"
foreground <- subset(markers$DEMs, cluster == foreground_group & logFC > 0)
foreground <- foreground[order(
    -foreground$mean_auc, -foreground$logFC,
    foreground$gene
), ]
genes_of_interest <- head(foreground$gene, 20)
head(foreground[, c("gene", "logFC", "mean_auc")])
result <- fishersPathwayAnalysis(
    Analyte = list(genes = genes_of_interest),
    universe = list(genes = rownames(rna)),
    pathway_index = pathway_index,
    min_path_size = 5, pval_cutoff = NULL
)
head(result[, c(
    "pathway_name", "analytes_in_pathways", "total_in_pathways",
    "fdr"
)], 2)
```

These enrichments summarize the selected markers of one archived cell-state
group. Foreground selection and testing use the same section, so the false
discovery rate (FDR) values describe this exploratory selection and require
independent validation.

## Identity counting and multiple testing

Foreground and universe share one identity index: memberships are united
across RaMP records and each gene counts once. In the displayed table,
`analytes_in_pathways` is the foreground-pathway overlap and `total_in_pathways`
is the pathway size within the measured background (M). The full result also
stores mapped foreground size (K) in `foreground_analytes_number` and mapped
background size (U) in `background_analytes_number`.

The universe is fixed before size filtering. Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) correction includes eligible
zero-overlap pathways; `pval_cutoff` filters afterward. Unresolved identifiers
are reported and excluded, so U counts resolved identities in the panel.

## Custom and species-specific references

Official resources harmonize human genes automatically. Custom bundles can
supply `gene_reference` or an explicit index; without a reference, they retain
RaMP-only mapping without downloading one. `gene_mapping = "ramp"` supports
historical or curated species-specific mapping. Orthology conversion requires
a separate step.
Identity reconciliation can change saved mappings and P values without
changing Fisher's calculation.

Share `pathway_index` between `findRegionalPathways()` and `pathwayNetworkPlots()`
to preserve identity and provenance.

# One membership index for enrichment, expression and plots

## Membership and coverage fields

`buildPathwayIndex()` joins identities to memberships. Its coverage fields are:

- `database_size`: reconciled, non-conflicting identities; `database_raw_size`:
  original RaMP records.
- `measured_size` and `coverage_fraction`: assay or measured-universe coverage.
- `used_size` and `used_members`: contributors after score or ranking filters.

A pathway score summarizes measured expression. Interpreting pathway activation
requires additional functional evidence.

## Shared memberships

When one gene has several RaMP records, the index unites their pathway
memberships and counts the gene once. Comparing `database_raw_size` (original
RaMP records) with `database_size` (reconciled identities) in the coverage
table below shows where this reconciliation applies.


## Pathway assays and spatial plots

We now reuse the 339-gene panel at the same 240 paired locations to map pathway
scores back to the tissue. The [joint analysis below](#joint-ms-and-rna-pathways)
then adds the measured MSI features. These locations provide spatial
observations within one specimen; biological replication requires independent
specimens.

`pathway_index` is shared across aggregation, scoring and plotting. `pathways`
stores scores; `coverage` records measured and excluded members. The two
prespecified Reactome pathways, **Neuronal System** and **Axon guidance**,
connect the targeted brain panel to neural function. Their exact RaMP IDs are
selected by name and source, then checked for at least five measured genes.

`plotPathwaysSpatially()` sums member log-normalized expression, divides by
the square root of member count, and standardizes each pathway across
locations. Figure 5.\@ref(fig:human-pathway-closure) displays the resulting
`pathway_maps` with a shared z-score colour bar; each map shows relative spatial
variation within its pathway.

```{r human-pathway-closure, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.6, out.width="860px", fig.cap="Prespecified Reactome Neuronal System and Axon guidance pathway scores at the same 240 aligned glioma locations. Scores use log-normalized RNA and retain the archived coordinates. A shared z-score colour scale (-3 to 3) shows relative spatial variation within each pathway; the titles identify the selected pathways."}
spe <- createPathwayAssay(spe,
    analyte_type = "genes", assay = "SPT",
    assayName = "logcounts", outputExperiment = "gene_ids",
    pathway_index = pathway_index, verbose = FALSE
)
spe <- createPathwayObject(spe,
    assay = "gene_ids", outputExperiment = "gene_pathways",
    pathway_index = pathway_index, min_path_size = 5, max_path_size = 500
)
pathways <- altExp(spe, "gene_pathways")
coverage <- pathwayMapping(pathways)$coverage
head(coverage[, c(
    "pathwayRampId", "database_size", "database_raw_size",
    "measured_size", "coverage_fraction", "excluded_conflict_count"
)])
selected <- coverage$pathwayRampId[coverage$eligible &
    coverage$pathwayName %in% c("Neuronal System", "Axon guidance") &
    coverage$type == "reactome"]
pathway_maps <- plotPathwaysSpatially(selected, spe,
    assay = "SPT",
    assayName = "logcounts", pathway_index = pathway_index, combine = TRUE
)
attr(pathway_maps, "pathway_coverage")[, c("pathwayName", "measured_size", "used_size")]
pathway_maps
```

## Duplicate features and audit outputs

Derived assays preserve the selected layer name, and original measurements
remain unchanged. Identical duplicate rows are removed; different rows mapping
to one gene require an explicit aggregation choice. Choose
`duplicate_genes = "mean"` for log-expression or `"sum"` when additive
measurements are appropriate for the analysis.
Use exact `pathwayRampId` values when display names are ambiguous.

Coverage is available in `attr(result, "pathway_coverage")`, pathway score
rowData/metadata, and plot attributes. Outputs retain reference fingerprints;
plots also return the displayed score vector. Complete audits include
unmeasured and conflict-only pathways even when no score is drawn.

# Joint MS and RNA pathways {#joint-ms-and-rna-pathways}

## Candidate identities and measured coverage

The same locations retain `r nrow(spe)` MSI features and `r nrow(rna)` RNA
features. We annotate the positive-mode MSI using CHCA and three prespecified
singly charged adducts: proton, sodium and potassium addition. Positive polarity
is recorded in the [original processing script](https://github.com/GenomicsMachineLearning/SpaMTP/blob/main/inst/Publication_Files/FigS6_script.Rmd).
The 5 ppm window and score floor of 0.05 define an exploratory candidate set.
`metabolite_ambiguity = "exclude"` removes features with competing RaMP compound
identities. Unique matches remain putative assignments requiring chemical
validation; the chosen adduct set defines the scope of that uniqueness.

The archived MS `counts` layer holds processed, spatially aligned abundances.
For this comparison, `LogNormalize` uses the total of the retained MS panel
at each location, with the same 10,000 scaling and `log2(1 + x)` transform as RNA.
Each modality is normalized separately.

The annotation summary reports reference formulae whose formula-based evidence
is unavailable; `annotationCandidates(spe)$FormulaStatus` records their status.

```{r human-joint-identities}
positive_adducts <- c("M+H", "M+Na", "M+K")
chem_index <- buildMZAnnotationIndex(database$chem_props,
    polarity = "positive", maldi_matrix = "CHCA", adducts = positive_adducts
)
spe <- annotateSM(spe,
    index = chem_index,
    assay = "main", raw.mz.column = "mz", ppm = 5,
    polarity = "positive", maldi_matrix = "CHCA", adducts = positive_adducts,
    min_score = 0, return.only.annotated = FALSE,
    save.intermediate = TRUE, verbose = FALSE
)
spe <- normalizeSMData(spe, "LogNormalize", assay = "main", verbose = FALSE)
spe <- createPathwayAssay(spe,
    analyte_type = "metabolites",
    assay = "main", assayName = "logcounts", outputExperiment = "compound_ids",
    annotation_score_threshold = 0.05, metabolite_ambiguity = "exclude",
    database = database, pathway_index = pathway_index, verbose = FALSE
)
compounds <- altExp(spe, "compound_ids")
compound_audit <- pathwayMapping(compounds)
retained_ms <- unique(unlist(compound_audit$original_features))
gene_status <- rowData(rna)$spamtp_gene_status
data.frame(
    stage = c(
        "Measured features", "Retained features", "Distinct identities",
        "Ambiguous/conflicting features", "Unmapped features"
    ),
    RNA = c(
        nrow(rna), sum(gene_status == "mapped"),
        nrow(altExp(spe, "gene_ids")),
        sum(gene_status == "conflicting_ramp_records"),
        sum(gene_status == "not_in_ramp")
    ),
    MS = c(
        nrow(spe), length(retained_ms), nrow(compounds),
        length(compound_audit$excluded_conflicts),
        nrow(spe) - length(unique(compound_audit$inputs$mz_name))
    )
)
```

`r length(retained_ms)` MSI features contribute `r nrow(compounds)` distinct
compound identities; `r length(compound_audit$excluded_conflicts)` features
have competing compound identities at the stated threshold. Multiple retained
features assigned to one compound are averaged before ranking. The unmatched MS count includes features with no RaMP candidate passing the
score floor; RNA exclusions are detailed in the mapping audit above.

## Complete ranks and modality contributions

We reuse the `Oligo` contrast. `findAllDEMs()` estimates every mapped gene's
and compound's regional effect, including negative effects, and
`findRegionalPathways()` ranks them for the `Oligo` region (`regions`). Joint
ranking root-mean-square (RMS) scales each modality's complete rank vector
before pooling. Pathways with 5–500 measured identities are tested; BH
correction covers the whole eligible family. The result reports measured and
leading-edge members of each modality; the table selects five pathways with
measured members from both modalities after testing.

```{r human-joint-pathways}
gene_markers <- findAllDEMs(spe,
    ident = "cout_labels", assay = "gene_ids",
    assayName = "logcounts", method = "markers", spatial_blocks = 0,
    verbose = FALSE
)
compound_markers <- findAllDEMs(spe,
    ident = "cout_labels", assay = "compound_ids",
    assayName = "logcounts", method = "markers", spatial_blocks = 0,
    verbose = FALSE
)
joint <- findRegionalPathways(spe,
    ident = "cout_labels",
    ranks = list(genes = gene_markers, metabolites = compound_markers),
    regions = foreground_group, pathway_index = pathway_index,
    rank_scale = "rms", min_path_size = 5, max_path_size = 500, verbose = FALSE
)
both <- joint[joint$measured_genes > 0 & joint$measured_metabolites > 0, ]
both <- both[order(both$padj, -abs(both$NES), both$pathwayRampId), ]
head(both[, c(
    "pathwayName", "NES", "padj", "measured_genes",
    "measured_metabolites", "leading_genes", "leading_metabolites"
)], 5)
```

Among `r format(nrow(joint), big.mark = ",")` tested pathways,
`r nrow(both)` contain measured members from both modalities;
`r if (sum(both$padj <= 0.05, na.rm = TRUE) == 0L) "none" else format(sum(both$padj <= 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), big.mark = ",")`
of these meet BH FDR <= 0.05. Of those `r nrow(both)` pathways,
`r sum(both$leading_genes > 0 & both$leading_metabolites > 0)` have leading-edge
members from both modalities. In the five displayed pathways,
`r sum(head(both$leading_metabolites, 5))` of
`r sum(head(both$leading_genes + both$leading_metabolites, 5))` leading-edge
members are compounds.

Positive normalized enrichment score (NES) indicates enrichment towards higher expression in the archived
`Oligo` group; negative NES indicates the opposite direction. Measured-member
and leading-edge counts show each modality's contribution after RMS rank
scaling. These exploratory rankings describe this single section's targeted
RNA panel and putative compound assignments.

## Compare regional pathway effects {#regional-pathway-plot}

`plotRegionalPathways()` displays up to eight joint Reactome pathways by
largest absolute NES, ordered by reference-membership overlap. Selection
leaves the BH adjustment across the full tested family unchanged.

```{r human-regional-pathway-plot, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=7, out.width="860px", fig.cap="Joint RNA/MSI pathways for Oligo. Colour shows NES, point area shows tested members, and a dark outline marks BH-adjusted P <= 0.05."}
both_reactome <- subset(both, type == "reactome")
plotRegionalPathways(both_reactome,
    num_display = 8, database = database)
```

## Explore a joint pathway network {#pathway-network}

We illustrate **Transport of small molecules** (Reactome `R-HSA-382551`),
chosen for coverage of both modalities without using its P value.
The network reuses the `Oligo` ranking and `pathway_index` above to place
measured gene and compound effects on archived interactions.

```{r human-network}
network_rows <- subset(joint,
    type == "reactome" & sourceId == "R-HSA-382551"
)
network_rows[, c("pathwayName", "NES", "padj",
    "measured_genes", "measured_metabolites")]
database$ramp_reactome <- loadSpaMTPDatabase("ramp_reactome",
    version = "3.0.7"
)$ramp_reactome
network_file <- pathwayNetworkPlots(spe,
    ident = "cout_labels", regpathway = network_rows,
    DE.list = list(genes = gene_markers$DEMs,
        metabolites = compound_markers$DEMs),
    selected_pathways = "R-HSA-382551",
    ST_assay = "gene_ids", stAssayName = "logcounts",
    SM_assay = "compound_ids", smAssayName = "logcounts",
    database = database, pathway_index = pathway_index,
    metabolite_detection = "annotated",
    max_nodes = 80, label_mode = "detected", layout_mode = "force",
    path = tempdir(), verbose = FALSE
)
attr(network_file, "network_summary")
```

The pathway contains `r network_rows$measured_genes` measured genes and
`r network_rows$measured_metabolites` putative compounds. Reference neighbours
and equivalent gene nodes make viewer counts differ from these identities.
`max_nodes` prioritizes leading-edge members and annotated compounds;
other measured genes can be pruned.

`embedPathwayNetwork()` displays the viewer below. **Download network HTML**
saves an offline copy; **Export SVG** saves the current diagram.

```{r human-network-viewer}
embedPathwayNetwork(network_file, height = 760,
    title = "Human glioma: Transport of small molecules"
)
```

Click a measured node to see its abundance at the 240 paired locations.
Use **Layout** and dragging to arrange the graph; **Fit view** shows all nodes.
**Details** opens the legends and spatial panel. Toggle
**Focused network** to change the visible reference context. This example
contains one pathway and one region.

| Display element | Interpretation |
|:--|:--|
| Circles and rectangles | Reference gene and metabolite nodes, respectively |
| Node colour | Descriptive regional expression effect; unavailable effects are grey |
| Purple outline | A member of the GSEA leading edge |
| Dark metabolite outline | An annotated pathway compound, including members outside the leading edge |
| Edge colour, line and arrow | Archived interaction type and direction; see the edge legend |
| Spatial abundance panel | The selected node's assay values at tissue coordinates, with its own scale and a plain background |

Node effects are descriptive contrasts within one tissue section. Pathway NES
and adjusted P values summarize the joint ranking; replicate-level inference
requires independent specimens. MSI identities are putative, and reference
neighbours include unmeasured nodes. Colours and outlines summarize these
associations; pathway activation requires functional evidence.

The paired maps show APOD RNA and the putative spermidine identity at the same
locations, providing a static view of these two network members.

```{r human-network-members, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=3.8, out.width="860px", fig.cap="APOD RNA and putative spermidine abundance at the same 240 paired locations. Each panel uses its own logcount scale. These single-section maps display the selected pathway members' spatial distributions."}
plotSpatialFeature(spe, c("RAMP_G_000005676", "RAMP_C_000000954"),
    assayName = "logcounts", ncol = 2,
    labels = c("APOD (RNA)", "Spermidine candidate (MSI)")
)
```

The filtered `compound_ids` assay has fixed identities, so annotation-score
controls are hidden. With scored mass-feature input, those controls filter
the exported overlay without recalculating enrichment.

## Find pathway co-regulation without region labels {#pathway-coregulation}

`runRAMPGeseca()` tests whether pathway genes co-vary across observations,
using RNA without region labels or spatial coordinates. We center each gene
and retain its variance (`scale = FALSE`), so high-variance genes can contribute
more. Pathways require 5–100 measured genes.

```{r human-pathway-coregulation}
gene_expression <- assay(altExp(spe, "gene_ids"), "logcounts")
coregulation <- with_seed(1234, runRAMPGeseca(gene_expression,
    pathway_index = pathway_index, minSize = 5, maxSize = 100,
    center = TRUE, scale = FALSE, eps = 0))
coregulation <- as.data.frame(coregulation)
coregulation$pathwayName <- database$pathway$pathwayName[
    match(coregulation$pathway, database$pathway$pathwayRampId)
]
head(coregulation[, c("pathwayName", "pctVar", "padj", "size")], 5)
```

`pctVar` is the variance captured by the aggregate pathway profile; `padj`
compares it with random sets from the measured panel after multiple-testing
adjustment. Interpret this covariance in the context of the targeted panel
and cell composition. Spatial autocorrelation and pathway activation require
separate assessment. Pathway names are reference labels; identical measured
gene sets can share results under different names.

Continue with [pathway resources](Pathway_Database_Integration.html) to inspect
the interaction evidence available for these memberships, or the
[complete workflow](End_to_End_Workflow.html) for spatial analysis and reports.
